newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Ciampi sees 15 trln lire mini-budget - paper.
newsitem.headline: Italy Ciampi sees 15 trln lire mini-budget - paper.

text.p: Italy's Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi is proposing a mini-budget to cut Italy's deficit by 15 trillion lire in the spring of this year, according to the financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore.

The paper quoting Treasury sources, said that the preliminary examination of the whole of 1997 showed the need for a mini-budget of 15 trillion lire in 1997. The budget measure will be considered in March at the end of the first quarter.

In an interview with daily Corriere dell Sera, Ciampi said that the Maastricht target of reaching a three percent deficit to GDP ratio in 1997 to qualify for European Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999 would be hard but not impossible to reach.
"It is a hard result but not impossible," Ciampi said about one of the financial target needed to be reached in 1997 to be among the first wave of European nations into EMU in 1999.

On the need for a mini-budget in 1997, Ciampi said, "We will see in the next few weeks if we need further measures for 1997." While on the prospects of bringing forward the 1998 budget he said this was a decision to be made by Prime Minster Romano Prodi, Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco and himself.
